properties.description: Platinum on tungsten trioxide composite, electrochromic electrode

nodes.name: WO3 Sputtering Deposition
nodes.procedure: WO3 film was deposited on the conductive ITO glass using a direct current (DC) magnetron sputtering technique under O2 atmosphere at room temperature.
nodes.source_text: WO3 film was deposited on the conductive ITO glass using a direct current (DC) magnetron sputtering technique under O2 atmosphere at room temperature.

nodes.name: Pt Photodeposition and Annealing
nodes.procedure: After that, the grown WO3 film was immersed into the diluted Pt (H2PtCl6·6H2O) solutions (30 mmol L^{-1}) under the radiation of xenon lamp at the wavelength of 200 - 400 nm for 2 h. Followed by the thermal treatment at 150^\circ C for 1 h under the vacuum condition, the resultant Pt@WO3 electrode materials were obtained for further measurements.

nodes.characterization_summary: No signals indicate the existence of WO3 and Pt nanocrystals on the XRD pattern of Pt@WO3 sample, suggesting the amorphous nature of WO3 film and supporting Pt layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of Pt@WO3 film was examined by the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern. In addition to the intrinsic peaks of underlying ITO-glass substrate, no signals indicate the existence of WO3 and Pt nanocrystals on the XRD pattern of Pt@WO3 sample (Figure S1, Supporting Information), suggesting the amorphous nature of WO3 film and supporting Pt layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of sputtered WO3 layer shows an additional shoulder peak at 950 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the W=O stretching vibration mode, evidencing the amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra further evidences the amorphous nature of the deposited WO3 layer. In contrast to the characteristic signals of well-crystallized tungsten oxides and typical bands (560 and 1100 cm⁻¹) of ITO glass (Figure S2, Supporting Information), the Raman spectra of sputtered WO3 layer shows an additional shoulder peak at 950 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the W=O stretching vibration mode (Figure S2b, Supporting Information), which can be attributed to the abundance of terminal O atoms in the amorphous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM characterizations reveal that Pt layer has been deposited on the flatten WO3 film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterizations reveal that Pt layer has been deposited on the flatten WO3 film (Figure 1b,c; Figures S3 and S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM characterizations reveal that Pt layer has been deposited on the flatten WO3 film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterizations reveal that Pt layer has been deposited on the flatten WO3 film (Figure 1b,c; Figures S3 and S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-magnification TEM image exhibits extensive amorphous Pt nanoparticles on tungsten-oxide matrix; average size of supported Pt nanoparticles is ≈3.14 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-magnification TEM image exhibits extensive amorphous Pt nanoparticles on tungsten-oxide matrix (Figure 1f), and the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern shows rather weak and broad diffraction ring corresponding to the (020) facet of WO3 substrate (Figure 1g), further suggesting the poor crystallization of these sputtering tungsten oxides and Pt deposition. The average size of supported Pt nanoparticles is determined to be ≈3.14 nm by statistic analysis (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows rather weak and broad diffraction ring corresponding to the (020) facet of WO3 substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern shows rather weak and broad diffraction ring corresponding to the (020) facet of WO3 substrate (Figure 1g), further suggesting the poor crystallization of these sputtering tungsten oxides and Pt deposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: The hierarchical structure of Pt and WO3 layers was identified by the STEM-EDS element mapping images.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The hierarchical structure of Pt and WO3 layers was identified by the STEM-EDS element mapping images (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: W 4f XPS peaks of fresh WO3 at 35.4 and 37.6 eV (W⁶⁺); Pt@WO3 shifts to 35.2 and 37.4 eV; O 1s shows lattice oxygen (530.4 eV), oxygen vacancy (531.6 eV), and H₂O_ads (532.6 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution W 4f XPS spectra of fresh WO3 sample show two peaks with binding energies at 35.4 and 37.6 eV, which can be attributed to the W 4f₇/₂ and W 4f₅/₂ of W⁶⁺ species, respectively. After the introduction of Pt component, these two W 4f XPS peaks slightly shift to low binding energies (35.2 and 37.4 eV Figure 4a)... Figure 4c shows the O 1s XPS profiles of fresh and used Pt@WO3 catalysts with fresh WO3 sample as a reference.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS measurements demonstrate fast charge-transfer kinetics for Pt@WO3 catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface (ECSA) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements demonstrate that Pt@WO3 catalyst surface possesses abundant active sites and fast charge-transfer kinetics during HER process, respectively (Figure 3e,f; Figure S16, Supporting Information).
